entries.title: Shop English: The Price on the Tag

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: The costume jacket says twenty dollars. Can I stop asking questions and pay now?

turns.speaker: Riley
turns.text: First ask: How much is it altogether? You want the total you actually need to pay.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: How much is it altogether? In this pretend shop, the assistant says twenty-two dollars, including a small extra charge.

turns.speaker: Riley
turns.text: Now you can decide before paying. Altogether asks for the total, not just the price of one part.

entries.prompt: Which question checks the total: What colour is it, or how much is it altogether?
entries.answer: How much is it altogether? Ask for the total before you pay.

entries.title: Disagree in English Without Judging Your Friend

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Your friend loves a mystery series. You watched two episodes and found them slow. Listen to two possible answers. First: Anyone who likes that show has terrible taste.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Second: I found the beginning slow. What did you enjoy about it? The second answer describes your own experience. It leaves room for your friend's different reaction, without pretending you liked the show.

entries.prompt: Which answer gives an opinion without judging the viewer: the first or the second?
entries.answer: The second. Say what you experienced, then ask a genuine question.

entries.title: Shop English: Ask Before You Remove the Tag

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: The jacket might be too small. I'll buy it and ask about returning it tomorrow, after the party.

turns.speaker: Riley
turns.text: Ask now: Can I return it if it doesn't fit? In our fictional shop, the assistant says yes, but only with the tag still attached.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: So yes doesn't mean I can wear it to the party, remove the tag, and bring it back later.

turns.speaker: Riley
turns.text: Right. The condition changes your choice. Ask the assistant to explain anything unclear before paying. Different shops may give different answers.

entries.prompt: In this pretend shop, what must stay attached if you may return the jacket?
entries.answer: The tag. Check the shop's stated conditions before you decide to buy.

entries.title: A Bad Review Is Not a Bad Evening
entries.hook: Dislike the film. Keep the friendship.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: Ethan's friend chose a film for their evening together. Ethan didn't enjoy the story, but he loved talking with her afterwards. When she asks about the film, he doesn't need to pretend.

turns.speaker: narrator
turns.text: He says: The film wasn't for me, but I enjoyed our evening. Those are two different experiences. An honest opinion about a film doesn't have to become a judgment of the person who chose it.

entries.prompt: Does Ethan dislike spending time with his friend, or just the film they watched?
entries.answer: Just the film. He enjoyed the evening and says so honestly. Separate the activity from the company.
